promptHead: Athlete goal: 5K (Corrowmore Harvest 5K) on Sun Nov 15 2026, 10 weeks out, target run the whole way.

new.headline: Strong first week: three runs done, no pain, heart rate under control. Keep the same three days next week and nudge each one slightly longer, with walking on the other days.

flags.title: Calf tightness
flags.detail: it eased by morning, but keep an eye on it as the runs get longer.

flags.title: Three-run rhythm
flags.detail: Mon, Wed, Sat is working, so protect the rest days between them.

flags.title: Walk-run intervals
flags.detail: still the right tool for 10 weeks out, do not drop them yet.

answers.question: I want to be ready for the 5K in November. Should I run every day next week to get there faster?
answers.answer: No, please do not run every day yet. Your body is brand new to this, and the gap days are where the fitness actually gets built. Three runs a week with easy walking in between will get you to Nov 15 safely; adding more days now is the fastest way to a sore shin or calf and a setback. We have ten weeks, which is plenty of runway for the goal of running the whole 5 km.

new.analysis:
The big win this week is simply that you started and finished three sessions with zero pain and a very steady heart rate. That is the foundation we build on, so the job for the week of Aug 31 is to repeat the pattern and add a small amount, not to reinvent it.

I am keeping your Mon, Wed, Sat run days and asking for a touch more time on each one, with Saturday as the longest. Heart rate stayed mostly in zone 2 with some zone 3, which is exactly where a beginner should be, so the same walk-run intervals of about 1 minute run and 90 seconds walk are fine to carry forward.

The other days are not empty. A gentle dog walk or a 20 to 30 minute easy walk on Tue, Thu and Sun helps recovery and adds aerobic time without pounding. Full rest on Friday sets up a good Saturday.

Calves were tight the day after each run, which is normal this early. Two things help: a slow 5 minute walk warm-up before each run, and a minute or two of easy calf stretching after. If any soreness sharpens into pain that gets worse day on day, back off and get it looked at.

safetyCallouts.title: Calf tightness is normal early on.
safetyCallouts.body: Warm up with a 5 minute walk, stretch gently after, and if soreness turns into pain that worsens day by day, pause running and see a physio.
